We study sleep, stress and emotions as life happens, and build interventions to help.



Especially for people affected by cancer. A lab in the School of Psychological Sciences and the Turner Institute for Brain and Mental Health at Monash University, led by Dr Joshua Wiley.

title: Joshua F. Wiley’s CV
text:
Academic summary




Associate Professor at Monash University; 11.3 years since PhD
More than $26 million AUD in grant funding as a chief investigator
Successfully graduated 11 primary doctoral students, 4 co-supervised doctoral students and 29 Honours students
Currently supervising 5 primary doctoral students, 4 co-supervised doctoral students, 3 Masters students and 1 Honours student
Former NHMRC Investigator Grant panel member (2019–2022)
45 first/last-author and 86 co-author peer-reviewed articles; 7 books; 25 other publications
163 publications in total (99 since the start of 2021)
26 first/last-author and 30 co-author peer-reviewed abstracts; 10 invited presentations
10 software packages developed (>970,000 CRAN downloads of 8 packages, Posit mirror, as of October 2026)
Served as Associate Editor of the International Journal of Behavioral Medicine (2019–2024), handling ~100 submissions

title: Our ethics and values
text:
The wellbeing and health of each member of our team and of the people who participate with us in our work, whether colleagues, study participants or consumer and community partners and advisors, is our first priority.
We are committed to creating an environment for work and study that is ethical, inclusive and supportive. All of us are responsible for upholding these core values, being constantly mindful of them, being accountable for our actions and decisions, and speaking up about any actions or decisions contrary to these values.
One concrete step we take to ensure we uphold these values is fostering transparency and open and safe communication across all team members.

title: Research
text:
We study how sleep, stress and emotions shape health and wellbeing in everyday life, and we develop practical, scalable ways to help, especially for people affected by cancer.
Our team is led by Dr Joshua Wiley and sits within the School of Psychological Sciences and the Turner Institute for Brain and Mental Health at Monash University, in the Sleep and Circadian Rhythms Program.


Research themes

Treating insomnia and fatigue (especially in cancer)
Psychosocial cancer care
Sleep in everyday life
Stress, coping and emotions
24-hour time use: sleep, activity and sitting
